name: Mount Ascutney Lookout (moved from its original spot)
summary: Mount Ascutney summit lookout: a 1940 steel tower later shortened to a 25-ft observation tower in the state park; the association's relocation claim is not confirmed by other sources.
design: Steel fire tower, 54 ft as built in 1940; today's observation tower is shorter (25 ft)
agency: Vermont Department of Forests, Parks & Recreation

access.note: Inside Mt. Ascutney State Park; summit reached by the paved Mountain Road and four trails. The sources give no rules for climbing the observation tower.

visit.trail_note: Four major trails, about 12 miles in total, start at the base and climb to the summit

events.note: Cabin and tower built on the mountain, per the 11th Biennial Report of the Commissioner of Agriculture as quoted by Forest Lookouts
Steel lookout tower, 54 ft, erected by a side camp from the Plymouth CCC Camp; a July 1940 newspaper credits the Civilian Conservation Corps
Light copper roofs blew off and were replaced with galvanized iron (report for the term ending June 30, 1942)
State park gives 1952 as the end of fire tower/lookout use
Vermont Forest Service biennial report for 1957-1958 says the Ascutney station was continued on an inactive basis
Former fire tower at the summit shortened and turned into an observation platform (date not given; described in a 2016 guide)
Association lists a relocated Mount Ascutney observation tower as standing; no source read describes the move
